answer: Split each vote into two steps and let beginners see the rule before it bites: first the juror marks the claim, then an audit re-runs a sample. Quorum spans subnetworks that share no operator, so a farm cannot fill a panel with its own keys, and a failed audit slashes the bond of the juror and the author together. The result is a slow market, since a diverse panel takes longer to fill. Some identities wander between panels without ever anchoring a case, which is fine as long as they keep staking. An opal of a clean sample proves one day, not one panel.
